dimensions.assessment: Directly affects broadband and telecommunications providers, railroad carriers, state and local governments, and the Federal Communications Commission.
dimensions.evidence: a broadband or telecommunications provider is seeking to place or modify equipment within a railroad carrier’s right-of-way

dimensions.assessment: Establishes fixed timelines, safety review standards, compensation rules based on actual costs, and a petition and adjudication process handled by the FCC.
dimensions.evidence: A carrier must approve or deny an application within 60 days of receipt

dimensions.assessment: Requires providers to pay railroad carriers for actual costs incurred and requires reimbursement of FCC expert service costs by the losing party in certain proceedings.
dimensions.evidence: pay the railroad carrier for actual costs incurred with respect to the application

dimensions.assessment: Amends Title VII of the Communications Act of 1934 to add a new section creating a federal review framework and mandating FCC rulemakings.
dimensions.evidence: Title VII of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 601 et seq.) is amended by adding at the end the following

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent statutory procedures and requires the FCC to issue implementing regulations within one year.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this section, the Commission shall promulgate regulations

missing_information: The aggregate monetary volume of fees or cost-reimbursements across all potential railroad corridors is not stated.
importance_detail.rationale: H.R. 6046 establishes a streamlined statutory and regulatory framework governing the placement and modification of broadband and telecommunications facilities in railroad rights-of-way and public-railroad intersections.
